Chapter 6: Navigating Turbulence—Crisis, Competition, and the Will to Win.
Have you ever felt like the ground was shifting under your feet? Every leader faces moments like that—when everything you thought you could count on suddenly feels uncertain. For this company, the late '80s and early '90s were exactly that.
Picture this: the economy is in a downturn, new competitors are popping up left and right, and the media is watching your every move. The old strategies just aren’t cutting it anymore, and the pressure to keep up is nonstop.
Inside the company, tension was thick. People worried about layoffs, wondered if their teams would make it, and questioned whether all those bold choices from the past would actually pay off. There’s this one meeting that really captures the mood—a group of managers, sitting around a scuffed-up conference table, faces tight with concern. The numbers aren’t good, and everyone can feel the weight of the outside world pressing in.
It would’ve been easy to pull back—to play it safe, hope things would blow over. But the leader? He wouldn’t let fear call the shots. Instead, he pushed for more honesty, quicker decisions, and a real willingness to tackle the tough stuff head-on. He’d walk the halls, listen to people’s worries, ask those hard questions, and always come back to this: “We can’t control the market, but we can control how we respond.”
One story from that time really sticks out. There was a team in a business unit on the brink of being sold off. Most folks might’ve given up, but not them. They dug deep, got creative, and started reimagining what their products could be. Night after night, they kept at it. And while the turnaround didn’t happen overnight, their grit paid off. Not only did the unit survive—it became a shining example of how determination and fresh thinking can spark a comeback.
What’s amazing is how crisis, even though it’s tough, can actually drive growth. The company learned to move faster, cut through red tape, and zero in on what truly mattered. Most people never realize how resilient they are until things get tough. But those years proved that being adaptable and having guts are just as important as having a good plan.
Through it all, the leader’s message was rock solid: “We’re in this together. We win as a team, or not at all.” That sense of unity—shaped by shared challenges—became one of the company’s greatest strengths.
